paragraphs.sourceText: Many people believe that passion and commitment are the foundations of strong romantic relationships. But a relationship is made of two 26 individuals. And the personality traits ( 4,H1) these individuals 27 or lack can often make a relationship more- or less- likely to 28 . Recent research has found that one trait in particular-humility ( ilil:D -is an important indicator of successful relationships.

Humility can sometimes be 29 with a lack of confidence. But researchers have come to realize that being humble generally indicates the 30 of deeply admirable personal qualities. Being humble means you have the ability to accurately 31 your deficiencies without denying your skills and strengths. For example, you might recognize that you are intelligent, but realize that you are not a 32 . Thus, humility leads to an honest view of one's own advantages and shortcomings. Humble people do not ignore, avoid, or try to deny their limits or deficiencies. They can 33 mistakes, see value in things that are far from perfect and identify areas for improvement.

Perhaps it is not 34 then, that humility appears to be a huge asset to relationships. One study found that people tend to rate this quality 35 in their spouse. The study also found that someone who is humble is more likely to initiate a romantic relationship, perhaps because they are less likely to see themselves as "too good" for someone else. Thus, a humble partner might be your ideal partner.

paragraphs.sourceText: There's a stress gap between men and women
paragraphs.translationZh: 男女之间存在压力差距

paragraphs.sourceText: A) "I used to work very hard. I love to create things, grow them and solve problems, "said Meng Li, a successful app developer in San Francisco. "I didn't really care about my mind and my body until they decided to go on strike."
paragraphs.translationZh: A) “我以前工作非常努力。我喜欢创造事物、培养它们并解决问题，”旧金山成功的应用程序开发人员李萌说。 “在他们决定罢工之前，我并没有真正关心我的思想和身体。”

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Ms. Li said her stress led to sleeplessness. When she did sleep, she experienced "problem-solving dreams," which left her feeling unrested when she woke up. "After I became a first-time mother, I quickly realized I was so busy caring for other people and work that I felt like I'd lost myself," she said.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 李女士说她的压力导致失眠。当她睡觉时，她会经历“解决问题的梦”，这让她醒来时感到不安。 “当我第一次成为母亲后，我很快意识到我太忙于照顾他人和工作，以至于我感觉自己迷失了自己，”她说。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) It's a common story- one we frequently ridicule and readily dismiss, for example, by claiming that women tend to complain more than men, despite the growing sum of research that underlines the problem. Women are twice as likely to suffer from severe stress and anxiety as men, according to a 2016 study published in The Journal of Brain & Behavior. The American Psychological Association reports a gender gap year after year showing that women consistently report higher stress levels. Clearly, a stress gap exists.
paragraphs.translationZh: C）这是一个常见的故事——我们经常嘲笑并轻易驳回这个故事，例如，声称女性比男性更容易抱怨，尽管越来越多的研究强调了这个问题。根据 2016 年发表在《大脑与行为杂志》上的一项研究，女性遭受严重压力和焦虑的可能性是男性的两倍。美国心理学会年复一年地报告了性别差距，表明女性始终报告更高的压力水平。显然，存在压力差距。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) "The difference is not really news to me, as a clinical psychologist," said Erin Joyce, a women and couples therapist in Los Angeles. "It's been well documented in extensive research over the years that prevalence rates for the majority of the anxiety disorders are higher in women than men." Some people may argue that this is merely reported data, and they say many men feel the same pressures as women in terms of fulfilling responsibilities at work and home. In other words, we're all really, really stressed.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）“作为一名临床心理学家，这种差异对我来说并不是什么新鲜事，”洛杉矶的女性和夫妻治疗师艾琳·乔伊斯说。 “多年来的广泛研究已经充分证明，大多数焦虑症的患病率在女性中高于男性。”有些人可能会说这只是报告的数据，他们说许多男性在履行工作和家庭责任方面感受到与女性相同的压力。换句话说，我们都非常非常有压力。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) "The difference, however, is in the nature and scope of these responsibilities in the home environment in particular," Dr. Joyce said. For example, the United Nations reported that women do nearly three times as much unpaid domestic work as men. The problem is, housework is often overlooked as work, even though it is often as laborious (or in some cases, more so) as any paid job. As the scholar Silvia Federici put it in 1975, the unpaid nature of domestic work reinforces the assumption that "housework is not work, thus preventing women from struggling against it."
paragraphs.translationZh: E）“然而，区别在于这些责任的性质和范围，特别是在家庭环境中，”乔伊斯博士说。例如，联合国报告称，女性从事的无酬家务劳动几乎是男性的三倍。问题是，家务劳动常常被当作工作而被忽视，尽管它通常和任何有偿工作一样费力（或者在某些情况下，更辛苦）。正如学者西尔维娅·费德里奇 (Silvia Federici) 1975 年所说，家务劳动的无偿性质强化了“家务劳动不是工作，从而阻止女性与之抗争”的假设。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) It's not just inside the home, though. Research from Nova Southeastern University found that female managers were more likely than male managers to display "surface acting," or forcing emotions that are not wholly felt. "They expressed optimism, calmness and sympathy even when these were not the emotions that they were actually feeling," the study said.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 不过，这不仅仅发生在家里。诺瓦东南大学的研究发现，女性管理者比男性管理者更有可能表现出“表面行为”，即强迫人们不完全感受到的情绪。研究称：“他们表达了乐观、冷静和同情，即使这些不是他们真正感受到的情绪。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Surface acting is a prime example of "emotional labor," a concept that the writer Jess Zimmerman made familiar in a 2015 essay. The essay sparked a massive thread on the internet community blog MetaFilter. Hundreds of women spoke up about their own experience with emotional labor: the duties that are expected of them, but go unnoticed. These invisible duties become apparent only when you don't do them. Like domestic labor, emotional labor is generally dismissed and not labeled work. But research shows it can be just as exhausting as paid work. Emotional labor can lead to difficulty in sleeping and family conflict. Sure, circumstantial stress, like losing a job, may lead to these same issues. But emotional labor is not circumstantial. It's an enduring responsibility based on the socialized gender role of women.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 表面表演是“情感劳动”的一个典型例子，作家 Jess Zimmerman 在 2015 年的一篇文章中熟悉了这一概念。这篇文章在互联网社区博客 MetaFilter 上引发了热议。数百名女性讲述了她们自己在情感劳动方面的经历：她们被期望承担但却被忽视的职责。只有当你不履行这些无形的职责时，它们才会变得明显。与家务劳动一样，情绪劳动通常被忽视，不被贴上“工作”的标签。但研究表明，这可能和有偿工作一样令人疲惫不堪。情绪劳动会导致睡眠困难和家庭冲突。当然，环境压力（例如失业）可能会导致这些相同的问题。但情绪劳动并不是偶然的。这是一项基于女性社会化性别角色的持久责任。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Like Ms. Li, many women try to manage the added stress to reach what Dr. Joyce said was an unattainable ideal. "Some professional women aim to do it all. They want to reach the top of the corporate ladder and fly like supermom," she said. When women don't reach this ideal, they feel guilty; and even more stressed. After her own struggle with this, Ms. Li took a step back and used her experience to build Sanity & Self, a self-care app and platform for overworked women. "The realizations I had in that process helped me gain insights and ultimately got me ready to integrate self- care into my daily life," she said.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 像李女士一样，许多女性试图控制额外的压力，以实现乔伊斯博士所说的难以实现的理想。 “一些职业女性的目标是做到这一切。她们希望达到企业阶梯的顶端，并像超级妈妈一样飞翔，”她说。当女性没有达到这个理想时，她们会感到内疚；甚至压力更大。在经历了自己的挣扎之后，李女士退后一步，利用自己的经验创建了 Sanity & Self，这是一款针对过度劳累女性的自我护理应用程序和平台。 “我在这个过程中获得的认识帮助我获得了见解，并最终让我做好了将自我保健融入日常生活的准备，”她说。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) The stress problem extends beyond mental health when you consider the link between stress, anxiety and heart health. Worse, most of what we know about heart disease comes from studies involving men. However, "there are many reasons to think that it's different in women," Harvard Medical School reported. For example, women are more likely to experience disturbed sleep, anxiety and unusual fatigue before a heart attack. Stress is so normalized that it is easy for women to shrug off those symptoms as simply the consequences of stress. Many women also do not experience chest pain before a heart attack the way men do, which leads to fewer women discovering problematic heart issues. Harvard reports that women are "much more likely than men to die within a year of having a heart attack" and "many women say their physicians sometimes don't even recognize the symptoms."
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 当你考虑压力、焦虑和心脏健康之间的联系时，压力问题不仅仅限于心理健康。更糟糕的是，我们对心脏病的了解大部分来自对男性的研究。然而，“有很多理由认为女性的情况有所不同，”哈佛医学院报告说。例如，女性在心脏病发作前更有可能经历睡眠不安、焦虑和异常疲劳。压力如此普遍，以至于女性很容易将这些症状视为压力的后果而忽视。许多女性在心脏病发作前也不会像男性那样经历胸痛，这导致更少的女性发现有问题的心脏问题。哈佛大学报告称，女性“心脏病发作一年内死亡的可能性比男性高得多”，而且“许多女性表示，她们的医生有时甚至没有意识到这些症状。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The good news is, women are more likely than men to take charge of their stress and manage it, the American Psychological Association reports. The concept of self-care, at its core, is quite simple. "The basics of adequate sleep, healthy diet and exercise are a good place to start," Dr. Joyce said. "Support from trusted relationships is vital. This includes professional support from various health and wellness providers if stress is becoming increasingly overwhelming."
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 美国心理学会报告称，好消息是，女性比男性更有可能掌控并管理自己的压力。自我保健的概念其核心非常简单。 “充足的睡眠、健康的饮食和锻炼是一个很好的起点，”乔伊斯博士说。 “来自值得信赖的关系的支持至关重要。如果压力变得越来越难以承受，这包括来自各种健康和保健提供者的专业支持。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Disconnecting from work and home responsibilities 1s also obviously important. But it's much easier said than done. It is important to understand what causes your stress in the first place. "Get really specific with what's stressing you out," Ms. Li said. "We often chalk up our stress to broad experiences like work. But work stress can take many different forms. Is a colleague being disrespectful of your time? Is a boss undermining your day-to-day control over decision making? These are different causes of stress and can benefit from different kinds of self-care." L ) Ideally, your spouse or partner will be supportive, rather than dismissive, of your stress. It is important to talk through these issues before they come to a head. "Women working outside of the home should make an effort to have a conscious conversation with their partners about more equitable sharing of household and family responsibilities," Dr. Joyce said.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 脱离工作和家庭责任显然也很重要。但说起来容易做起来难。首先了解造成压力的原因很重要。 “具体说明是什么给你带来了压力，”李女士说。 “我们经常将压力归因于工作等广泛的经历。但工作压力可以有多种不同的形式。同事是否不尊重你的时间？老板是否破坏了你对决策的日常控制？这些是压力的不同原因，可以从不同类型的自我保健中受益。” L ) 理想情况下，你的配偶或伴侣会支持你，而不是轻视你的压力。在这些问题达到紧要关头之前讨论清楚是很重要的。 “在外工作的女性应该努力与伴侣进行有意识的对话，以更公平地分担家庭责任，”乔伊斯博士说。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Some career women who aim high tend to feel guilty if they fail to achieve their goals.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 一些目标远大的职业女性如果未能实现目标，往往会感到内疚。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. The unpaid housework done by women is triple that done by men.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 妇女承担的无偿家务劳动是男性承担的三倍。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. It is reported that women consistently suffer more from severe stress than men.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 据报道，妇女始终比男子承受更多的严重压力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Women are advised to identify the specific causes of their stress so that steps can be taken to deal with it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 建议妇女查明造成压力的具体原因，以便采取措施应对。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. One study showed that women managers often expressed positive emotions that they didn't really feel.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 一项研究表明，女性管理者经常表达出她们并未真正感受到的积极情绪。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Women tend to mistake signs of heart attacks for symptoms of stress.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 女性往往将心脏病发作的迹象误认为是压力症状。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. For a time an app developer in America was so busy attending to work and family that she suffered from sleeplessness.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 美国的一位应用程序开发人员一度忙于工作和家庭，以至于失眠。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. The emotional labor women do is noticed only when it is not done.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 女性所做的情感劳动只有在没有完成时才会被注意到。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Dr. Joyce suggests that apart from self-care, women should seek professional support if they experience severe stress.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 乔伊斯博士建议，除了自我护理外，女性在承受严重压力时还应该寻求专业支持。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Some people believe that there may not exist a stress gap between men and women.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 有些人认为，男性和女性之间可能不存在压力差距。

For each of them there are four choices marked AJ, BJ, CJ and DJ. You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 AJ、BJ、CJ 和 DJ。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: As many office workers adapt to remote work, cities may undergo fundamental change if offices remain under-utilized. Who will benefit if working from home becomes the norm?
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着许多办公室工作人员适应远程工作，如果办公室仍未得到充分利用，城市可能会发生根本性变化。如果在家工作成为常态，谁会受益？

paragraphs.sourceText: Employers argue they make considerable savings on real estate when workers shift from office to home work. However, these savings result from passing costs on to workers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 雇主们辩称，当员工从办公室转向在家工作时，他们可以在房地产方面节省大量资金。然而，这些节省是由于将成本转嫁给工人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Unless employees are fully compensated, this could become a variant of parasitic (寄生的) capitalism, whereby corporate profits increasingly rely on extracting value from the public- and now personal- realm, rather than on generating new value.
paragraphs.translationZh: 除非员工得到充分补偿，否则这可能成为寄生资本主义的一种变体，企业利润越来越依赖于从公共领域（现在是个人领域）提取价值，而不是创造新价值。

paragraphs.sourceText: Though employers are backed by a chorus of remote work advocates, others note the loneliness, reduced productivity and inefficiencies of extended remote work.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管雇主得到了远程工作倡导者的一致支持，但其他人也指出了长期远程工作带来的孤独感、生产力下降和效率低下。

paragraphs.sourceText: If working from home becomes permanent, employees will have to dedicate part of their private space to work. This requires purchasing desks, chairs and office equipment.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果在家工作成为永久性的，员工将不得不腾出部分私人空间来工作。这就需要购买办公桌、椅子和办公设备。

paragraphs.sourceText: It also means having private space dedicated to work: the space must be heated, cleaned, maintained and paid for. That depends on many things, but for purposes of illustration, I have run some estimates for Montreal. The exercise is simple but important, since it brings these costs out of the realm of speculation into the realm of meaningful discussion.
paragraphs.translationZh: 它还意味着拥有专用于工作的私人空间：该空间必须加热、清洁、维护并付费。这取决于很多因素，但出于说明目的，我对蒙特利尔进行了一些估计。这个练习很简单但很重要，因为它将这些成本从猜测领域带入有意义的讨论领域。

paragraphs.sourceText: Rough calculations show that the savings made by employers when their staff works from home are of similar value to the compensation workers should receive for setting up offices at home.
paragraphs.translationZh: 粗略计算显示，雇主在员工在家工作时节省的费用与员工在家设立办公室应获得的报酬相当。

paragraphs.sourceText: What does this mean for offices in cities? One of two things may happen: Employers pass these costs onto employees. This would be a form of expropriation ( 1! Ji ), with employees absorbing production costs that have traditionally been paid by the employer. This represents a considerable transfer of value from employees to employers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这对于城市办公室意味着什么？可能会发生以下两种情况之一：雇主将这些成本转嫁给雇员。这将是一种征用形式（1！Ji），员工承担传统上由雇主支付的生产成本。这代表着相当大的价值从雇员到雇主的转移。

paragraphs.sourceText: When employees are properly compensated, employers' real estate savings will be modest. If savings are modest, then the many advantages of working in offices-such as lively atmosphere, rapidity of communication, team-building and acclimatization ( it EL J;f- .t;t) of new employees-will encourage employers to shelve the idea of remote work and, like Yahoo in 2013, encourage employees to work most of the time from corporate office space.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当雇员得到适当的补偿时，雇主的房地产储蓄将是有限的。如果节省的资金不多，那么在办公室工作的许多优势——例如气氛活跃、沟通迅速、团队建设和新员工的适应能力（it EL J;f-.t;t）——将鼓励雇主搁置远程工作的想法，并像 2013 年的雅虎一样，鼓励员工大部分时间在公司办公空间工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: The human thirst for knowledge is the driving force behind our successful development as a species. But curiosity can also be dangerous, leading to setbacks or even downfalls. Given curiosity's complexity, scientists have found it hard to define.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人类对知识的渴望是我们作为一个物种成功发展的驱动力。但好奇心也可能是危险的，会导致挫折甚至失败。鉴于好奇心的复杂性，科学家发现很难对其进行定义。

paragraphs.sourceText: While pinning down a definition has proven tricky, the general consensus is it's some means of information gathering. Psychologists also agree curiosity is intrinsically (内在地) motivated.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然确定一个定义很棘手，但普遍的共识是它是某种信息收集方式。心理学家也同意好奇心是内在驱动的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Curiosity covers such a large set of behaviors that there probably isn't any single "curiosity gene" that makes humans wonder about and explore their environment. That said, curiosity does have a genetic component. Genes and the environment interact in many complex ways to shape individuals and guide their behavior, including their curiosity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 好奇心涵盖了如此多的行为，以至于可能没有任何单一的“好奇心基因”使人类对他们的环境产生好奇和探索。也就是说，好奇心确实有遗传成分。基因和环境以许多复杂的方式相互作用，塑造个体并指导他们的行为，包括他们的好奇心。

paragraphs.sourceText: Regardless of their genetic makeup, infants have to learn an incredible amount of information in a short time, and curiosity is one of the tools humans have found to accomplish that gigantic task.
paragraphs.translationZh: 无论其基因构成如何，婴儿都必须在短时间内学习大量信息，而好奇心是人类发现的完成这项艰巨任务的工具之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: Hundreds of studies show that infants prefer novelty. It's what motivates non-human animals, human infants and probably human adults to explore and seek out new things before growing less interested in them after continued exposure.
paragraphs.translationZh: 数百项研究表明婴儿更喜欢新奇事物。它促使非人类动物、人类婴儿甚至成年人探索和寻找新事物，然后在持续接触新事物后对它们失去兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: But curiosity often comes with a cost.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但好奇心往往是有代价的。

paragraphs.sourceText: In some situations, the stakes are low and failure is a healthy part of growth. For instance, many babies are perfectly proficient crawlers, but they decide to try walking because there's more to see and do when they stand upright. But this milestone comes at a small cost. A study of 12- to 19-month-olds learning how to walk documented that these children fell down a lot. Seventeen times per hour, to be exact. But walking is faster than crawling, so this motivates expert crawlers to transition to walking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在某些情况下，风险很低，失败是成长的一个健康组成部分。例如，许多婴儿非常擅长爬行，但他们决定尝试走路，因为当他们直立时可以看到更多东西，做更多事情。但这一里程碑的代价很小。一项针对 12 至 19 个月大的孩子学习走路的研究表明，这些孩子经常摔倒。确切地说，每小时十七次。但步行比爬行更快，因此这促使爬行专家过渡到步行。

paragraphs.sourceText: Sometimes, however, testing out a new idea can lead to disaster. For instance, the Inuit people of the Arctic regions have created incredible modes to deal with the challenges of living in northern climates, but what we forget about are the tens of thousands of people that tried and failed to make it in those challenging landscapes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，有时，测试一个新想法可能会导致灾难。例如，北极地区的因纽特人创造了令人难以置信的模式来应对北方气候下生活的挑战，但我们忘记的是成千上万的人在这些充满挑战的环境中尝试过但失败了。
